summary: The product's own checks, run exactly as the product runs them: its typecheck (server, orchestrator, web), its end-to-end smoke test on an embedded throwaway Postgres (every MCP tool, the worker API, scoring, API-key auth, the landing page and access requests, ending in its per-tool tenant-isolation sweep: every MCP tool called as a second organisation with every identifier of the first), and its MCP connector check against the deployed address.
not_covered: The smoke test runs on this machine against an embedded Postgres, not against the deployed database: it proves the code, and the deployed stack is graded by the mcp.check row and the deploy's own health step.
mcp.check calls the read-only tools only (the product's own scripts/mcp-check.ts): it never launches a simulation or spends inference.
Signed-in pages (/admin, /app) behind the product's own sign-in provider are not driven by any row here.

checks.run: npm run typecheck; s=$?; rm -f web/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo; exit $s

checks.name: smoke
checks.run: d=$(mktemp -d) && env -u DATABASE_URL -u CLICKHOUSE_URL PGLITE_DIR="$d" npm run smoke; s=$?; rm -rf "$d"; exit $s

requires.else: Install the product's own dependencies into the snapshot's ignored folders (no lockfile is written there): npm --prefix molds/mold_v0/codebase ci && npm --prefix molds/mold_v0/codebase/orchestrator ci && npm --prefix molds/mold_v0/codebase/web install --no-package-lock

stdout: isolation sweep: [0-9]+ tools x [0-9]+ argument sets

checks.why: The product's own `npm run smoke`, which must reach its last section, the per-tool isolation sweep; a failure is the product's own assertion, quoted in the output.

checks.name: mcp.check
